scenario_metadata.notes: Illustrative synthetic scenario data. Tariff baseline/spike figures are grounded in real 2025-2026 Section 301 semiconductor tariff policy (25% -> 50% doubling precedent, further escalation actions in motion); all other figures (costs, capacities, transport costs, facility fixed costs) are invented for modeling purposes and are not sourced from real supplier contracts.

demand_generation_methodology.description: Both historical_demand_last_8_weeks and actual_demand_ground_truth_by_week are generated the same way: weekly_demand (the fixed baseline) multiplied by a noise factor drawn from a uniform distribution on [0.8, 1.2] (i.e. +/-20%), rounded to a whole unit. The demand-spike disruption (week 6, C5, x1.5) is layered multiplicatively on top of this noise for that specific customer-week only. Generated ONCE via a seeded random process, then frozen -- identical for every participant and every forecasting method, exactly like the disruption schedule. Actual demand is intentionally generated independently of any forecasting method's prediction: forecasting methods are scored on how well they predict this fixed, pre-existing ground truth from historical data alone, not the other way around. This preserves comparability across participants and keeps the solve-once-per-forecasting-method Oracle architecture valid, since every method faces the same underlying reality.

network_design_reference_solution.description: Brute-force-verified optimal answer for Stage 0 (Network Design), used as ground truth to validate the Oracle's network design output before trusting it.

runner_up.note: Only $8 more expensive than the true optimum -- intentionally close, so a participant reasoning by intuition could plausibly (and defensibly) land here instead.

per_period_cost_parameters.note: Holding/backorder rates are deliberately stylized/compressed for whole-number player readability within a 10-week horizon; they are not derived from a literal real-world annualized inventory carrying cost percentage.

disruption_schedule.description: Overseas Manufacturer's tariff temporarily escalates from 50% to 100% for this week only, pushing landed cost from $15 to $20 per unit -- temporarily more expensive than Domestic Fab ($18).
C5's demand temporarily increases by 50% for this week only.
Overseas Manufacturer's capacity at every facility is temporarily cut by 50% for this week only.
